- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., >0.2), model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day forecasts — if recent 5-day average is >10% above forecast, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend, model tends to drift upward; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid false momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early divergence (first 5 days), model often misses downward correction; apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
